name: Gelatinous Drop-Like Corneal Dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Gelatinous Drop-Like Corneal Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic subepithelial gelatinous amyloid deposits in the cornea confirmed by Congo red staining
Multiple translucent, gelatinous, drop-like nodules on the corneal surface visible on slit-lamp examination
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the TACSTD2 gene

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical appearance and histopathological confirmation of amyloid deposits
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can support diagnosis but is not mandatory; family history may be absent in sporadic cases.

laboratory: Congo red staining positive for amyloid deposits in corneal biopsy
imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing gelatinous drop-like nodules
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (OCT) showing subepithelial deposits
other: Family history consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Linear amyloid deposits rather than gelatinous nodules
Later onset and different genetic mutations (TGFBI gene)
Non-amyloid deposits with characteristic map, dot, and fingerprint patterns
Lack of gelatinous nodules and amyloid staining

redFlags: Recurrent corneal erosions with severe pain
Signs of secondary infection or corneal perforation
references: Kobayashi A, et al. Gelatinous drop-like corneal dystrophy: clinical and molecular genetic studies. Ophthalmology. 2000.
